question.name: Question 7
question.problem: Consider the closed curve $C,$ which is the boundary of the region enclosed by $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $y=0.$ Express ${∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-y)\,dx+(2x-{y}^{2})\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14120089/assets/a3fe0bbc283a2eaacffad4b6be071f601781b6b77b2df0dd9b30abb22653c738.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={x}^{2}-y$ and $Q(x,y)=2x-{y}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,0\le y\le 1-{x}^{2}}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({x}^{2}-y)\,dx+(2x-{y}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2-(-1))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
